speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for over three weeks now. It's mostly dry, but sometimes I cough up a little white phlegm, and I've noticed I get quite short of breath when I try to walk or do any physical activity. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration suggests a subacute process; have you noticed any fever, chills, or night sweats accompanying the cough and breathlessness? Also, do you have a history of smoking or recent exposure to dust or chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or night sweats. I used to smoke a pack a day for thirty years but quit ten years ago, and I don't think I've been exposed to any dust or chemicals recently. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of heavy smoking is significant even after quitting. Do you experience chest pain, palpitations, or swelling in your legs and ankles? Also, does your cough worsen when you lie down flat?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't have any chest pain, my heart rate feels normal, and my legs aren't swollen. The cough doesn't seem to get worse when I lie down flat.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with chronic bronchitis.
